newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine estimates 355,000-365,000 T cotton lint.
newsitem.headline: Argentine estimates 355,000-365,000 T cotton lint.

text.p: Argentine farmers should produce 355,000-365,000 tonnes of 1995/96 cotton lint if the weather holds out well for the rest of the harvest, the government's Agriculture Secretariat said Friday.
Of 952,000 hectares sown, some 894,000 hectares are fit to harvest, which should give raw cotton output of 1.08-1.15 million tonnes, the Secretariat said.
Some 15,000 tonnes of the raw cotton should be exported for processing to Paraguay, and the rest used to produce lint in Argentina.
But the Secretariat added that final output "will depend on the weather conditions, when the first frosts come, and pest control during the rest of 1996/97."
Some 443,000 tonnes of raw cotton had been harvested by May 2.
Rafael Almiroty, of exporters Almiroty y Compania, told Reuters Monday that he thought the drought-hit crop would probably only produce about 300,000 tonne of lint.
Farmers sowed over 900,000 hectares with 1996/97 cotton, down from a record 1.0 million hectares last season but still well above the historical average. Last year's lint output was 425,000 tonnes.
